data.title: Why is CZ expecting limited Bitcoin downside from the $6.3B Binance hack?
data.description:
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) has echoed ongoing discussions that the $6.3B hack won’t negatively impact Bitcoin’s value. According to CZ, the Binance exploit’s exposure to BTC is relatively small, 18,270 BTC compared to Mt. Gox’s 650,000 BTC. 

That’s less than 1%, while Mt. Gox’s exploit involved 5% of the total BTC supply.

CZ added, 

Number of users impacted, and % of user assets impacted. Mt. Gox (the largest CEX at the time) and FTX (not small) were all near 100% of users and their assets.

Finally, CZ noted that whether the affected platform covers all the losses dictates the market sentiment. Binance has already reserved $6.34B to cover the losses and has begun buying some of the stolen assets to refund users. 

Will Binance hack confirm Bitcoin’s cycle bottom?

When news of the exploit was first reported on Thursday, Bitcoin dropped by 4% from $81.9K and closed at $77.9K. At the time of writing, the asset’s price hovered around $77.3K, down about 6% since the hack. 

According to Anthony Pompliano, the muted reaction to the largest hack in crypto history meant the market outlook was positive. 

One of the largest crypto exchanges gets hacked for $6 billion, and Bitcoin sold off less than 5%? Bullish.

Pompliano added that in the past, similar hacks triggered 20%-40% Bitcoin drawdowns. That’s not all either as he also drew some interesting parallels to FTX’s implosion, which marked 2022’s BTC cycle bottom around $16K.

He added, 

If you had purchased Bitcoin at the bottom, you would have seen your ~ $16,000 Bitcoin price turn into $125,000 over the next three years. The facts of this situation, and the muted price drawdown, tell me that investors should be gearing up for higher prices in 2027.

For his part, Ryan Watkins, founder of crypto VC firm Syncracy Capital, stated that the hack was the climax of the price pullback.

According to him, the incident helped reset and clear the remaining market froth (excess leverage). 

It’s possible we see more volatility over the coming weeks as the market digests the hack and rising macro uncertainty. This looks like the necessary reset I was looking for in what I believe is an early bull market.

Bitcoin’s Open Interest (OI), which tracks derivatives demand, leverage, and market froth, also dropped to $24B, from a recent peak of $27B when BTC’s price hit $87K. 

The cryptocurrency is now down 12% from its September high, but is yet to break below the 200-day MA ($73K) and the 50-week MA( $75.75K).

In other words, the early bull market cycle setup may still be intact. However, breaking below the two moving averages ($75K/$73K) would flip BTC back to bear market territory. 

Final Summary

  • CZ claimed BTC has seen a muted price drawdown because Binance will cover all losses tied to the $6.3B hack.
  • The incident offered a needed reset in market leverage, but cracking below $73K would invalidate the early bull market cycle setup

data.title: Bitcoin whitepaper turns 18, but what are the challenges ahead for BTC’s $1.6T market?
data.description:
It has been 18 years since Satoshi Nakamoto’s Bitcoin whitepaper was released on 31st October, 2008. The idea was simple – Offer an exit hatch from the traditional financial system with a peer-to-peer (P2P) money network with a fixed supply (21M coins) and no central control. 

Interestingly, the timing was not coincidental. It was just over two months after the U.S government committed to bailing out major banks after the 2008 financial crisis using taxpayers’ money. 

That meant massive money printing and hyperinflation and a decline in citizens’ purchasing power and wealth. In fact, Satoshi captured this frustration in a message on the first genesis Bitcoin block, which he mined himself on 23rd January 2009. 

The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.

18 years later, the banks Satoshi rebelled against are now adopting Bitcoin. Whether that is good or bad is debatable. Over the years, though, various narratives have shaped adoption and softened even some of Bitcoin’s once-vocal critics. 

What has changed after 2 decades?

Satoshi moved on to other things in early 2011, and BTC hit $1 that year. By 2025, the crypto’s price had rallied to a record $126K per coin on the back of increasing adoption by nation-states and companies as a sovereign global reserve asset. 

In fact, the world’s largest asset manager, BlackRock, initially labelled it a scam but later made a U-turn. In the last two years, BlackRock has pitched the $1.6T BTC market as digital gold and as a hedge against fiscal debt and geopolitical risks. 

Interestingly, U.S Spot BTC ETFs, led by BlackRock, now hold 1.6M BTC, the highest among institutional investors and nation-states. Public companies come in second at 1.265M BTC, with governments closing the top three list with 645.6K BTC. 

In particular, the UAE’s sovereign funds reported nearly $800M in BTC exposure in Q3, citing it as a strategic diversifier. This echoed BlackRock’s pitch.

As it stands, U.S fiscal debt is at +$40T and climbing. The EU and other jurisdictions are trying to stop P2P transfers. This has further cemented BTC’s original value proposition: a non-sovereign, censorship-resistant asset and hedge.  

In fact, even the BIS has acknowledged that BTC adoption highlights the level of distrust in traditional monetary systems and central banks. Interestingly, the BIS has called on central banks to modernize to counter BTC’s influence. 

Saumya Saxena, Global Builders Lead at Base, Coinbase, shared a similar position with AMBCrypto. 

Its (Bitcoin’s) significance goes beyond its scarcity; it represents a check and balance in the monetary system, demonstrating how competition can strengthen choice and trust.

What’s next for Bitcoin?

Right now, the network is facing security uncertainty from miners and post-quantum preparedness. Miners partly help secure the network, but their block rewards have dropped from 50 BTC to 3.125 BTC.

MARA thinks a further drop in rewards after the 2028 halving might make mining unsustainable.  

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin whitepaper turned 18 amid elevated fiscal debt, corruption, and geopolitical instability. 
  • Despite institutional adoption, Bitcoin faces security risks from miner exits and AI/quantum computer threats.

data.title: BEAM’s price defies market trends with multi-month uptrend, but what should traders do?
data.description:
Gaming sector and ecosystem token Beam [BEAM] has rallied by 45.2% in the last 24 hours, with a 1,115% hike in daily trading volume. The $241.6 million market cap asset has been trending higher since July.

While the rest of the crypto sphere panicked and sold after news of the Binance heist broke, BEAM’s price surged across the board.

This relative strength was likely due to its existing bullish momentum. It was reported that the Beam Foundation had burned all the BEAM tokens in the possession of the Binance hacker.

984.249 million tokens worth around $3.37 million were burned using the Gnosis Safe Burn Signature, which also helped explain the short-term bullish outlook.

BEAM continues its multi-month uptrend

In June, BEAM broke above the downtrend’s lower high at $0.0016, flipping its structure bullishly. The latest bullish continuation came when the $0.00356-high, made on 23rd October, was breached on the 30th.

The breakout was on extraordinary volume and the gains continued at the time of writing. Relative to the rest of the market, the latest bullish impulse move was highly noticeable.

It is likely the altcoin may be overextended. The RSI on the daily chart was at 82, once again in overbought territory. This does not mean a pullback will immediately follow though. A stretch of ovebought RSI readings earlier in October came alongside a 16.54% move higher over ten days.

Traders’ call to action – Take profits and wait for a pullback

The 4-hour chart showed that there were two support zones of interest right now. The first was at $0.00445, which was respected over the past 24 hours as a demand zone and the altcoin went to challenge the $0.0054 local highs.

The other support zone to watch was the $0.0034 order block that initiated this move higher.

Swing traders can think about taking profits and waiting for a pullback, or moving their trailing stop loss order to just below $0.0034, as per their preferred strategy.

A pullback towards $0.0040 would likely provide a buying opportunity. However, without a clear sign of a short-term pullback, BEAM swing traders need to wait and not rush to look for a re-entry.

Final Summary

  • BEAM token has been on an uptrend on the daily timeframe since June.
  • Latest impulse move higher has not settled into a pullback yet, and swing traders can choose to wait for a revisit of key demand zones before buying.

data.title: How Useless Coin’s 10% crash puts the $0.13 demand zone at risk
data.description:
Useless Coin [USELESS] has taken a big hit as the general crypto records a week of bearish advances. The token prices have dropped by more than 10% over the last 24 hours at press time, amid negative on-chain sentiments.

The token is trading below its key EMA and on the verge of breaking below the demand zone at around $0.13.

With the token leveraged position shrinking and significant unmitigated liquidity clusters lying below the current trading price, could the current bearish run be prolonged? 

Useless Coin faces mounting selling pressure

Useless Coin has followed the bearish trend witnessed across the majority of altcoins as they reap from the recent unchanged FOMC rates this week.

The token has since recorded significant bearish advances to test the current demand zone that sits between $0.125 and $0.145 as negative on-chain sentiment reinforces concerns about demand.

At the time of writing, the token was trading below all its key Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs) on the daily chart, leaving the short-term technical structure also tilted toward sellers. These EMAs could act as overhead resistance if the token attempts a recovery.

But with buyers having defended the zone on several occasions, this time it could follow the same trajectory. Notably, buyers have started to show up on short time frames.

Shrinking leveraged positions signals reduced volatility

On the derivatives, the token’s Open Interest has shrunk to just $32 million as of writing. This points to declining leveraged positions as traders and investors scale back their exposure as uncertainty increases.

At the same time, an unmitigated liquidity cluster worth $586K lies around 0.112. This highlights the price level as a key target for the network sellers before further bullish advances can be resumed.

In the past, similar zones acted as magnets to Useless’ price action. Moreover, the chances of the same repeating still remain high.

Can USELESS avoid further bearish push?

USELESS remains vulnerable while it trades below its key EMAs and tests the demand zone between $0.125 and $0.145. A successful defense could provide a base for recovery, particularly if broader market sentiment improves.

However, a decisive breakdown below $0.13 would strengthen the bearish outlook. Without renewed buying pressure, sellers could retain control and extend the decline.

As it stands, the $0.13 zone is the level to watch. Its ability to attract buyers could determine whether USELESS stabilizes or enters another phase of losses.

Final Summary

  • USELESS has dropped by more than 10% in the last 24 hours as negative on-chain sentiment and broader market weakness weigh on its price.
  • The network’s shrinking leveraged positions add to uncertainty as the token approaches the $0.13 demand zone, where a breakdown could expose it to further losses.

data.title: ‘Crypto moves forward regardless’ – Why Grayscale is looking past the U.S. midterms
data.description:
Grayscale’s Head of Research Zach Pandl believes that the cryptocurrency industry will continue to expand regardless of the outcome of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections.

In a report published on the 28th of October, Pandl argued that even if Democrats gain control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, the broader outlook for digital assets is unlikely to change significantly.

Zach Pandl’s bullish crypto market prediction

Currently, Republicans hold majorities in both chambers. However, prediction markets suggest that Democrats could take control after the elections.

Such a political shift could influence the regulatory environment for cryptocurrencies, particularly as the industry has benefited from greater regulatory clarity recently.

Furthermore, the years under Joe Biden offer sufficient evidence of a challenging cryptocurrency market. Despite this uncertainty, Pandl believes three major factors will support the industry’s long-term growth.

Factors driving Pandl’s prediction

According to Pandl, cryptocurrency is no longer associated with a single political party.

Research from Pew Research and The Harris Poll suggests that similar proportions of Republicans and Democrats own or use digital assets. Furthermore, legislation such as the GENIUS Act received bipartisan support in Congress, demonstrating that lawmakers from both parties recognize the importance of regulating and developing the sector.

He also highlighted the growing U.S. national debt as a long-term driver of cryptocurrency adoption. This is what Pandl believes would encourage investors to explore alternative stores of value, including Bitcoin [BTC] and other digital assets, as part of their broader investment strategies.

Main players in the U.S. crypto market

That said, Pandl also argued that the cryptocurrency industry does not depend exclusively on the United States. According to Grayscale’s estimates, only 15-20% of global crypto activity takes place in the U.S., while the remaining 80-85% happens internationally.

Hence, Pandl put it best when he said,

Regardless of the outcome of the US midterms, users around the world will continue to seek out alternatives to fiat currencies as well as more effective payment systems, and foreign regulators will continue to put in place rules to support digital assets innovation in their jurisdictions.

Crypto market dynamics paint a confusing picture

Well, the current crypto market dynamics also suggest the same, as the global cryptocurrency market capitalization stood at $2.71 trillion at press time, representing a 1.6% increase over the last 24 hours. Meanwhile, Bitcoin‘s market dominance stood at 60.30% at the time of reporting.

Additionally, the 24-hour trading volume reached $162.455 billion, up 120.9%. However, the market sentiment remains cautious as the Crypto Fear & Greed Index has dropped to 30, indicating ‘fear,’ compared with 51 (neutral) a day ago, 50 last week, and 71 (greed) last month.

This suggests that despite the increase in market capitalization, investors remain uncertain about near-term market conditions.

Lastly, AMBCrypto’s recent report also suggested that Bitcoin’s much-anticipated “Uptober” rally has disappointed investors, with BTC declining 4.2% month-to-date as of 25th October, against its historical average October return of 18.1%.

Still, all of these are mixed sentiments, which suggest that the market is still uncertain with no clear signs of what comes next.

Final Summary

  • At present, Republicans hold majorities in both chambers, but prediction markets suggest that Democrats could take control following the elections.
  • Only 15-20% of global crypto activity takes place in the U.S., while the remaining 80-85% happens internationally.

data.title: ‘Only 5 other times this decade’ – Why Bitcoin’s latest drop stands out
data.description:
The Binance hack has reignited discussions about Bitcoin’s [BTC] ability to recover from major security incidents and financial crises. While the latest breach triggered significant selling pressure, historical data suggests that Bitcoin has often demonstrated resilience following similar events.

According to an infographic shared by Rand Group, Bitcoin has historically recorded substantial gains in the 12 months following major crypto-related disasters. For instance, following the Mt. Gox hack in November 2011, BTC gained approximately 500% over the next year.

Similarly, Bitcoin rallied 160% after the January 2015 post-Mt. Gox collapse and 125% following the December 2018 crypto winter bottom.

The recovery was even stronger after the March 2020 COVID-19 market crash, with BTC gaining approximately 1,100% over the subsequent 12 months. Meanwhile, Bitcoin advanced 130% in the year following the November 2022 FTX collapse.

Execs weigh in on the same

David Lawant, head of research for Anchorage, also echoed the same when he said,

Historically, bitcoin has treated hacks and solvency events very differently: thefts tend to be absorbed within hours, while insolvencies are not.

According to his analysis, cryptocurrency thefts are often absorbed by the market within hours, whereas exchange failures and insolvencies tend to create more prolonged uncertainty.

His data examines Bitcoin’s price movements during the first 8.5 hours following selected incidents, separating exchange hacks, bridge and protocol exploits, and financial collapses. Lawant also argued that such incidents have limited predictive value for Bitcoin’s longer-term direction, which depends more heavily on the broader market cycle.

Not everyone shares the same sentimnet

However, opposing the above observations, Adam Livingston, Vice President, Investments at Strive, noted that Bitcoin experienced a 6.9% decline between the 29th and 30th of October, following the Binance-related panic.

Against its relatively low 30-day volatility of 1.3%, this represented a 5.3-standard-deviation move. It ranked among the most extreme two-day declines since 2020.

He added,

A drop this deep out of a market this quiet has happened only 5 other times this decade.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin has historically recorded substantial gains in the 12 months following major crypto-related disasters.
  • An exec also argued that such incidents have limited predictive value for Bitcoin’s longer-term direction.

data.title: Ethereum whales withdraw $29M despite bearish signals – Will ETH recover?
data.description:
Ethereum [ETH] whales have intensified their accumulation activity despite broader market weakness, withdrawing millions in ETH from exchanges. As per Lookonchain, two whale wallets received 13,002 ETH, worth roughly $29.09 million, from FalconX and OKX.

Specifically, one whale received 9,625 ETH worth nearly $21.57 million from FalconX, while a newly created wallet withdrew 3,377 ETH worth approximately $7.52 million from OKX.

These significant ETH withdrawals highlighted a growing interest among the large investors despite Ethereum’s recent price weakness.

Beyond the reported whale transfers, Ethereum’s broader exchange activity revealed token withdrawals despite prevailing market uncertainty. At the time of reporting, ETH  had recorded around -$35.45 million in Spot Netflow, according to CoinGlass data.

The negative reading implied withdrawals exceeded deposits, extending the broader trend of ongoing exchange outflows. The latest reading notably followed several considerable withdrawal spikes throughout October, an activity that could reduce immediately available selling supply.

However, these outflows are yet to translate into a meaningful price recovery, leaving Ethereum vulnerable to further declines.

Why are Ethereum traders turning increasingly bearish?

Contrastingly, while the Spot exchange withdrawals suggested potential accumulation, Ethereum’s derivatives market, on the other hand, reflected an opposite shift in trader positioning. CoinGlass highlighted that ETH’s OI-Weighted Funding Rate rapidly declined to -0.0097% as of writing.

Notably, the decline marked a sharp reversal from the predominantly positive funding rates recorded throughout the month of October. The reversal meant that the short traders paid long traders, highlighting growing demand for bearish exposure across leveraged positions.

Furthermore, the decline also suggested that the market participants highly anticipated further downside despite substantial whale withdrawals.

However, it is worth noting that the negative funding alone could not validate additional losses, particularly in case renewed buying triggers short liquidations.

Could $2,200 support spark ETH’s next rebound?

Ethereum’s daily chart structure highlighted a persistent bearish pressure as the token traded around $2,240 at press time, within a descending channel.

Notably, the bears had already pushed Ethereum beneath the $2,300 price level, weakening its previous support structure. More importantly, the price subsequently approached the $2,200 potential support, where buyers faced another crucial test.

The RSI indicator, meanwhile, dropped to 29.78 into oversold territory, implying intense selling pressure. Additionally, the MACD indicator  also maintained a bearish outlook below its signal line with its negative histogram confirming that sellers continued controlling the broader trend.

Ultimately, Ethereum’s $29.09 million whale accumulation and persistent exchange outflows offered potential recovery signals, but the prevailing bearish conditions continued limiting immediate recovery attempts.

For a sustained price rebound,  buyers would need to defend the $2,200 support and reclaim the $2,300 price level.

Final Summary

  • Ethereum whales withdrew $29.09 million in ETH as exchange outflows continued.
  • ETH approached $2,200 support, where buyers could likely attempt a recovery despite bearish indicators.

data.title: XRP exchange reserves drop by 250M tokens – Is a price recovery ahead?
data.description:
XRP exchange reserves have dropped across major trading platforms, with Binance recording its lowest holdings since December 2022 amid sustained withdrawals.

Between the 28th and 30th of October, Binance reserves reportedly declined 8.18%, dropping from 2.69 billion to 2.47 billion XRP. Additionally, Bybit, on the other hand,  registered a 6.54% decline, losing 20 million XRP as reserves fell to 286 million.

Furthermore, Bithumb followed with a 10 million XRP reduction, bringing its holdings to 1.837 billion XRP. The three exchanges combined lost 250 million XRP, potentially reducing the supply readily available for selling.

This broader reserve decline raised questions about whether the shrinking exchange supply could support XRP’s price recovery.

Spot outflows reinforce the declining reserve trend

In addition to declining reserves, XRP‘s Spot market experienced continued exchange outflows, further signaling the withdrawal trend. According to CoinGlass, XRP had registered $5.78 million in spot net outflows at the time of writing.

Notably, the netflows were negative for most of the recent trading period, with occasional inflows. This persistent withdrawal reduces exchange-held balances, potentially limiting the amount of tokens available for immediate selling.

However, the continued outflows didn’t necessarily signal higher demand, especially given the headwind of XRP’s recent losses.

XRP’s NVT collapse signals changing network activity

Meanwhile, XRP’s on-chain valuation metrics witnessed a drastic change as the exchange reserves kept declining.

The Network Value to Transactions (NVT) ratio plunged 54.77% over 24 hours as of writing, reaching 54.69. The drastic drop suggested that transactions were growing stronger than XRP’s prevailing market capitalization.

This development implied an expanding network utilization relative to valuation, even though the ratio alone could not confirm undervaluation.

More importantly, the higher relative transaction activity provided another possible basis for recovery, alongside the declining exchange reserves. However, XRP still had to gain more buying momentum to capitalize on these moves and push prices higher.

XRP defends support, but bears threaten recovery

Despite the supportive supply-side developments, XRP’s technical structure continued reflecting bearish pressure following its recent decline.

On the daily timeframe chart, the bulls decisively defended the $1.23 support level, allowing XRP to rebound toward $1.24. The Relative Strength Index indicator, however, remained weak at 36.55 at press time, below its Moving Average of 40.19.

Furthermore, the Money Flow Index (MFI) stabilized around 42.31, implying that buying pressure was yet to regain dominance. However, XRP’s declining exchange reserves and persistent outflows introduced potential support for a recovery attempt. 

The weak technical indicators continued threatening immediate gains, but maintaining the $1.2352 could help buyers challenge higher price levels.

Final Summary

  • XRP exchange reserves declined by 250 million tokens across Binance, Bybit, and Bithumb.
  • XRP defended $1.23 support, but weak indicators threatened a stronger price recovery.

data.title: CLARITY Act back in the spotlight after $6.3B Binance hack — Here’s why!
data.description:
The $6.3 billion Binance hack, the largest crypto security incident on record, has sparked fresh debate over cryptocurrency regulations in the United States, particularly the need for stronger safeguards for crypto exchanges.

According to Senator Cynthia Lummis, the incident highlights why the proposed CLARITY Act is important for the industry’s future.

Lummis blames the CLARITY Act setback

The Senator argued that the legislation would have provided crypto firms with legal clarity to freeze suspicious transactions as soon as law enforcement agencies flagged them. This would have allowed exchanges to respond immediately to potential security threats, rather than lose valuable time navigating regulatory uncertainty.

Lummis added, 

Every minute lost is money gone for good.

Lummis also warned that hackers stole more than $6 billion in less than four hours, making the incident larger than the previous two biggest crypto thefts combined — the $3.5 billion LuBian hack in December 2020 and the $1.4 billion Bybit exploit in February 2025.

CFTC Chairman stresses on new crypto regulations

At the same time, CFTC Chair Mike Selig also used the incident to reinforce the need for a federal registration framework for crypto exchanges. He argued that offshore exchanges lack the cybersecurity safeguards expected of regulated U.S financial markets.

However, his remarks were focused on vulnerabilities in supporting infrastructure, such as an individual’s laptop, rather than weaknesses in blockchain networks or smart contracts. 

Additionally, he also highlighted how blockchain transparency could help regulators trace stolen funds, even when hackers use privacy tools such as Tornado Cash. 

Selig went on to say, 

I think the fact that we can trace transactions on-chain, even when some of these technologies are used to obfuscate that, gives us a lot of potential as a regulator to be really a cop on the beat.

This is evidence that the Binance hack is particularly alarming. Especially since the amount affected already exceeds the combined value of the next nine largest crypto hacks, according to Glassnode. 

Crypto market faces the brunt

Here, it’s worth pointing out that the impact has also extended beyond just security concerns, weighing on market sentiment and liquidity.

According to DefiLlama, DeFi Total Value Locked (TVL) dropped by 5.3% on 30th October to $83.95 billion, its lowest level since 21st August. Stablecoin supply also declined to $296.6 billion, remaining below the $300 billion-mark since 24th October.

Meanwhile, around $1.5 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated as Bitcoin [BTC] briefly fell to $76,400, triggering widespread selling across major cryptocurrencies.

While Pepe [PEPE], Sky [SKY], and Bitcoin Cash [BCH] posted gains, riskier assets such as MemeCore [M], Ethena [ENA], and Pump.fun [PUMP] recorded significant losses.

Therefore, going forward, $76,400 remains a crucial support level for Bitcoin, while reclaiming $80,000 could signal improving market sentiment. On the other hand, a break below $76,000 could extend the broader risk-off trend.

However, with Binance expecting to resume withdrawals within 48 hours (from the day the hack was reported), hope remains.

Final Summary

  • Senator Lummis is the latest to comment on the Binance hack and what could have been done to prevent it. 
  • DeFi TVL dropped by 5.3% to $83.95 billion, while stablecoin supply also fell to $296.6 billion.

data.title: How can PEPE traders take advantage of conflicting momentum signals?
data.description:
At the time of writing, PEPE was down 2.50% in the last 24 hours, its performance noticeably worse than other leading memecoins. For its part, Dogecoin [DOGE] was down by only 0.94%, while Shiba Inu [SHIB] gained by 1.13%.

And yet, the memecoin has rallied by 7.42% over the past week. In fact, Glassnode data also showed that the memecoin sector, as a whole, has shed 3.1% of its value over the past week, less than BTC’s 4.4% or ETH’s 5.9%.

Does PEPE have a longer-term bullish bias, and should swing traders and investors be looking to buy? Here’s what you need to know!

PEPE bulls battle for control of Value Area High

The 1-day chart revealed a bullish swing structure in place. The key levels to watch were $0.0000032 and $0.00000536. A daily session close above $0.00000536 would confirm a bullish trend continuation.

Within this swing move, the Fixed Range Volume Profile tool was used.

It plotted the Value Area Low and High at $0.00000377 and $0.00000491, meaning 70% of the trading volume since 11th September, when the impulse move began, has taken place within these two levels. This also makes them important horizontal levels to watch.

The A/D indicator fell to new lows following the heavy selling on 29th October. Meanwhile, the Awesome Oscillator stayed above the zero line.

These conflicting signals did not seem to subtract from the overall bullish price bias PEPE showed on the daily timeframe. However, ideally, buyers would want to see sustained demand to keep the uptrend going.

PEPE swing traders can maintain a bullish bias

Over the past week, PEPE has oscillated between $0.0000042 and $0.0000056, and at the time of writing, was at the mid-range level. The technical indicators were neutral, with a slight bearish leaning from the Awesome Oscillator.

Traders and long-term investors can stay bullish given the daily timeframe structure, but should be prepared for a price dip toward $0.0000044 or even $0.0000038. Especially if Bitcoin faces intense selling pressure.

Final Summary

  • PEPE has shed more value in the past 24 hours than some of the larger crypto memecoins.
  • Swing traders and investors can maintain a bullish bias as the price challenges the VAH once again.
